speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help you safely, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located, how severe it is on a scale of 1 to 10, and if it radiates to your arm, jaw, or back?

REQUEST TEST: ECG
REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The ECG and basic metabolic panel results are normal, which helps rule out a heart attack and severe electrolyte imbalances. To better understand your vomiting, have you noticed any specific foods or substances that seem to trigger the episodes, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome (MWS). The history of forceful retching followed by sudden chest pain and choking, combined with normal cardiac workup, is highly suggestive of a gastric mucosal tear at the gastroesophageal junction. I am requesting images of the upper GI tract to confirm the presence of a tear or active bleeding. REQUEST IMAGES: Upper_GI_Series.
